blockingFindings.title: Reader accepts invalid Activity order and parses the unconfirmed ledger tail
blockingFindings.issue: readConfirmedLedger reads and validates the entire ledger buffer before slicing the confirmed prefix, so malformed or partial unconfirmed data can reject an otherwise valid query. It also never verifies contiguous confirmationOrder values, allowing a confirmed line with an arbitrary order to be projected.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Read only the byte range needed for the confirmed prefix and require each parsed Activity to have confirmationOrder equal to its 1-based prefix position.
blockingFindings.rationale: The canonical query must be bounded to confirmed evidence and preserve journal ordering; the current implementation can both reject valid prefixes and expose inconsistent cursor/order data.

blockingFindings.title: Artifact catalog validation omits canonical association and coverage checks
blockingFindings.issue: readCatalog checks descriptor content hashes and only tests that activityId values exist in the parsed prefix. It does not verify Activity ownership, authority-slot relationships, logical content contracts, or that all catalog-managed files are represented.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Use a shared canonical catalog verifier bound to the confirmed Activity index, including managed-file coverage, descriptor verification, and assertRelatedArtifact/content-contract checks before projection.
blockingFindings.rationale: A rehashed but semantically false catalog can currently produce incorrect public artifact, node, and Activity relationships while being reported as canonical.

blockingFindings.title: AggregateMetrics is emitted as an object literal
blockingFindings.issue: metrics returns a plain object assembled inline rather than a dedicated AggregateMetrics value class with the required exact keys, constructor invariants, and toJSON behavior.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Introduce an AggregateMetrics class with the exact contract keys and use it from QueryProjector.metrics() and metadata projection.
blockingFindings.rationale: T-1 explicitly requires AggregateMetrics to be a dedicated centrally managed class, and the project rules require meaningful structured values to own their invariants and behavior.

blockingFindings.title: Metric sums can become unsafe integers or JSON null
blockingFindings.issue: The unchecked reduce in metrics can exceed Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER for token/duration totals or become Infinity for large finite costs. JSON serialization converts Infinity to null even though measured values exist.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Use checked accumulation that rejects non-finite or unsafe totals as canonical inconsistency, or otherwise enforce a documented aggregate bound before returning a non-null metric.
blockingFindings.rationale: Aggregate values are required to be non-negative integers or finite numbers with null reserved for absent measurements; valid individually bounded Activities can currently violate that contract in aggregate.

blockingFindings.title: Several public collections and strings bypass bounded limits
blockingFindings.issue: relationships.taskNodes is built directly from every task without uniqueLimited(), and ActivityItem exposes unbounded failure, blocker, incomplete, metric, note, and nested artifactRefs values without the public collection/string limits.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Apply the centralized collection and string bounds to taskNodes, artifactRefs, incomplete.resources, metric/note/failure/blocker fields, rejecting canonical inconsistency rather than truncating or emitting oversized values.
blockingFindings.rationale: The public response can exceed the contract’s per-collection and per-string limits before the final response-size check, defeating the bounded-resource guardrail.

blockingFindings.title: CanonicalFlowVersionReader does not validate specRoot
blockingFindings.issue: The exported reader stores constructor-provided specRoot without normalization or validation, and listAvailableVersions() joins it directly. A value containing parent segments can make discovery read outside repositoryRoot.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Validate specRoot at CanonicalFlowVersionReader construction with the same normalized POSIX-relative-path invariant used by FlowVersionLocation, and reject absolute or parent-segment values.
blockingFindings.rationale: Reader discovery is a canonical repository boundary; path traversal can expose unrelated directories as available Flow Versions.

blockingFindings.title: sennel flow query bypasses worktree-local CLI resolution
blockingFindings.issue: The query branch exits before executeWorktreeLocalCli(). When a globally linked CLI is invoked from another worktree, query runs the wrong checkout and does not receive the worktree SENNEL_WORK_ROOT/SENNEL_SOURCE_ROOT bindings used by normal commands.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Add a query-specific worktree-aware source/root handoff after request boundary validation, preserving query isolation while ensuring the selected worktree implementation and canonical root are used.
blockingFindings.rationale: The same public command can read a different repository/version depending on how the CLI was launched, violating deterministic request handling and canonical selection.

blockingFindings.title: Contract limits and error codes are not shared with fixture and consumer compatibility artifacts
blockingFindings.issue: The diff centralizes limits and error codes only in src/flow/query.js; it adds no query fixture or consumer compatibility test that imports and verifies the same contract source.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Add the required fixture and consumer compatibility artifact, both importing the centralized request/response/error/limit contract used by the CLI, and assert exact keys, cardinality, and boundary limits.
blockingFindings.rationale: T-1 acceptance explicitly requires the error-code and collection/byte-limit contract to be shared across the CLI, fixture, and consumer compatibility test.

blockingFindings.title: Reader accepts invalid Activity order and rejects partial unconfirmed tails
blockingFindings.issue: readConfirmedLedger rejects any ledger whose final bytes do not end in a newline, even when the confirmed prefix is valid and the trailing line is unconfirmed. It also never requires each parsed Activity to have confirmationOrder equal to its 1-based prefix position.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Read and validate only the bounded confirmed prefix, tolerate an incomplete unconfirmed tail, and require contiguous confirmationOrder values for every confirmed entry.
blockingFindings.rationale: The query must expose only confirmed canonical evidence and preserve journal ordering; the current implementation can reject valid data or project inconsistent cursor/order values.

blockingFindings.title: Artifact catalog validation omits canonical association and coverage checks
blockingFindings.issue: readCatalog validates descriptor hashes and only checks that activityId values exist in the parsed prefix. It does not verify Activity ownership, authority-slot relationships, content contracts, or that every catalog-managed file is represented.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Use the canonical catalog verifier bound to the confirmed Activity index, including managed-file coverage, descriptor verification, assertRelatedArtifact checks, and content-contract association validation.
blockingFindings.rationale: A rehashed but semantically false catalog can currently produce incorrect public artifact, node, and Activity relationships while being reported as canonical.

blockingFindings.title: AggregateMetrics is emitted as an object literal
blockingFindings.issue: metrics returns a plain object assembled inline rather than a dedicated AggregateMetrics value class with the required exact keys, constructor invariants, and toJSON behavior.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Introduce an AggregateMetrics class with the exact contract keys and use it from QueryProjector.metrics().
blockingFindings.rationale: T-1 explicitly requires AggregateMetrics to be a dedicated centrally managed class, and the project rules require meaningful structured values to own their invariants and behavior.

blockingFindings.title: Metric counter reset and delta semantics are not implemented
blockingFindings.issue: QueryProjector.metrics() reads only Activity usage and timing. It never consumes activity.metric, so record_metric counter deltas are neither applied after reset nor guarded against duplicate accounting with usage.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Aggregate confirmed record_metric observations through a single counter state keyed by phase/counter, reset the baseline when reset is true, add each post-reset delta once, and keep usage-based token/cost measurements on a separate non-overlapping path.
blockingFindings.rationale: The task implementation notes make reset-aware record_metric aggregation and no double counting an explicit metric contract requirement.

blockingFindings.title: Page and recordedAt accept fields outside the request whitelist
blockingFindings.issue: QueryPage and DateRange destructure only known properties but never reject unknown ones. Consequently requests such as page:{limit:10,extra:true} or recordedAt:{gte:null,lt:null,extra:true} are accepted instead of failing the exact request contract; explicit null page/recordedAt values are also coerced to empty objects by QueryRequest.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Add exact-key validation inside QueryPage and DateRange, and reject null when the property contract requires an object rather than treating it as omitted.
blockingFindings.rationale: T-1 requires exact whitelist, type, and nullability enforcement at the centrally managed query boundary.

blockingFindings.title: Artifact descriptor records are normalized instead of checked for exact fields
blockingFindings.issue: readCatalog checks the catalog envelope keys, but FlowArtifactCatalog/FlowArtifactDescriptor silently ignore unknown keys on each descriptor. A catalog containing extra descriptor fields can therefore pass validation and be projected as if it were canonical.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Validate every raw descriptor against the query ArtifactDescriptor whitelist before constructing FlowArtifactDescriptor, and reject unknown, missing, or incorrectly nullable fields with a canonical inconsistency error.
blockingFindings.rationale: The task requires the ArtifactDescriptor schema and exact whitelist to be centrally enforced; silently dropping fields makes the accepted canonical record broader than the defined contract.

blockingFindings.title: MetadataItem, ActivityItem, and query ArtifactDescriptor remain ad hoc object literals
blockingFindings.issue: The response contract values are assembled as unvalidated object literals in metadataItem(), artifactDescriptor(), and activityItem(). They have no dedicated constructors, exact-key invariants, or value-owned serialization behavior.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Define query-specific MetadataItem, ActivityItem, and ArtifactDescriptor classes with constructor validation and toJSON(), then make QueryProjector return those typed values.
blockingFindings.rationale: T-1 requires these query-specific contract types, and the repository's mandatory OOP rule requires meaningful structured values to be represented by dedicated classes rather than object literals.

blockingFindings.title: Metrics aggregation ignores record_metric reset and delta semantics

blockingFindings.issue: When resource is not metadata or activities, QueryRequest fails before retaining the resource and runFlowQueryCli emits only schemaRevision, ok, and error. It omits the resource-specific error fields and does not define selectedFlowVersion nullability for the unknown-resource case.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Add a dedicated unknown-resource response contract with the required exact keys, stable error code/path, and selectedFlowVersion:null semantics.
blockingFindings.rationale: The acceptance criteria require both known-resource and resource-unknown error payload shapes to be explicitly defined.

blockingFindings.title: Pagination and date-range filters accept unknown fields and non-object values
blockingFindings.issue: QueryPage and DateRange destructure their inputs without exact-field checks. Consequently page.foo and recordedAt.foo are silently accepted, and arrays or null values can be treated as empty filter objects through the nullish defaults.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Require plain objects when page or recordedAt is present and reject every nested field outside the centrally defined whitelist.
blockingFindings.rationale: T-1 requires exact request whitelists and fixed types; silently discarding caller-supplied fields makes the request contract ambiguous.

blockingFindings.title: Aggregate metrics reads the wrong canonical usage source
blockingFindings.issue: QueryProjector.metrics() aggregates only activity.usage, while normal agent measurements are persisted by record_metric in activity.metric.tokens, activity.metric.cost, and activity.metric.durationMs. Consequently metadata metrics omit confirmed token, cost, and measured agent-duration data and do not apply reset/delta semantics.

blockingFindings.rationale: The acceptance criteria require resource-specific error payloads and defined selectedFlowVersion nullability, including request-validation failures.

blockingFindings.suggestion: Apply the shared collection-limit helper to taskNodes, outcome.artifactRefs, and every other public array before projection, failing with the canonical bounded-record error when a limit is exceeded.
blockingFindings.rationale: The query contract requires bounded public collections; relying only on the overall response byte limit does not enforce the declared per-collection contract.

blockingFindings.rationale: T-1 calls for query-specific classes/schema, and the project OOP rule requires meaningful structured values to enforce invariants through dedicated classes.

blockingFindings.issue: ActivityItem exposes unbounded failure, blocker, incomplete, metric, note, and nested artifactRefs values; taskNodes and several nested collections are not checked against the public limits.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Apply centralized string and collection limits at every public projection boundary, including nested observation fields, resources, artifactRefs, taskNodes, and identifiers.
blockingFindings.rationale: The response can exceed declared per-field and collection limits before the final response-size check, violating the bounded-resource guardrail.

blockingFindings.title: CanonicalFlowVersionReader does not validate specRoot
blockingFindings.issue: The reader stores constructor-provided specRoot without validation, and listAvailableVersions() joins it directly, allowing parent segments to discover versions outside repositoryRoot.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Validate specRoot as a normalized POSIX-relative path in the reader constructor, rejecting absolute paths and parent segments.
blockingFindings.rationale: Version discovery is a canonical repository boundary; path traversal can expose unrelated directories as available Flow Versions.

blockingFindings.title: Known-resource request errors lose the resource-specific response shape
blockingFindings.issue: request is assigned only after QueryRequest construction succeeds. A known metadata or activities resource with an invalid condition, page, or date range therefore falls into the generic error branch and omits resource, selectedFlowVersion, item/items, and pageInfo.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Retain the validated resource discriminator before full request construction and emit the appropriate typed known-resource error envelope with explicit selectedFlowVersion nullability.
blockingFindings.rationale: The acceptance criteria require distinct known-resource error payloads and defined selectedFlowVersion behavior.

blockingFindings.title: Activities queries omit confirmed Activities without timing
blockingFindings.issue: The activities filter always requires entry.timing.finishedAt, even when no recordedAt range is supplied, so confirmed Activities whose nullable timing is null are never returned.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Include every confirmed Activity when no date range is requested, and apply recordedAt filtering only to entries with usable timing evidence.
blockingFindings.rationale: The resource is defined over the confirmed Activity prefix, and Activity timing is nullable in the canonical model.

blockingFindings.title: Shared fixture and consumer compatibility artifacts are absent
blockingFindings.issue: The diff centralizes limits and error codes only in src/flow/query.js; it adds no fixture or consumer compatibility artifact that imports and verifies the same request, response, error, and limit contract.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Add the required fixture and consumer compatibility test, both importing the centralized contract source and asserting exact keys, cardinality, and boundary limits.
blockingFindings.rationale: T-1 explicitly requires the error-code and collection/byte-limit contract to be shared across the CLI, fixture, and consumer compatibility test.

blockingFindings.title: Metadata projection crashes on ordinary Activities
blockingFindings.issue: metrics() tests metric?.counter !== null; for a null metric this is true because undefined !== null, then metric.phase throws. Normal Activities commonly have metric=null, so metadata queries fail.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Guard the metric object before reading counter, for example require metric !== null && metric !== undefined before processing counter fields.
blockingFindings.rationale: A valid canonical Flow cannot produce the required metadata response when its confirmed Activities omit metric observations.

blockingFindings.title: Artifact catalog verification passes the wrong index type
blockingFindings.issue: readCatalog passes FlowArtifactActivityIndex to catalog.verify(), but FlowArtifactCatalog.verify() only accepts FlowArtifactActivityIndexFile. Every catalog read therefore throws the integrity-validation error.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Use the supported activity-index-file verifier over the confirmed prefix, or add a typed verifier that accepts the already parsed confirmed Activity index while retaining coverage, ownership, authority-slot, and content-contract checks.
blockingFindings.rationale: Valid canonical catalogs cannot be queried, and the required confirmed-Activity association checks are not successfully executed.

blockingFindings.title: AggregateMetrics violates the exact contract
blockingFindings.issue: AggregateMetrics includes an extra counters key, while the required exact key set excludes it. Several provenance values also differ from the required exact strings, such as confirmed-activity-metric-or-timing instead of activity-timing-durationMs.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Make AggregateMetrics validate and serialize exactly the ten required fields, remove counters from the public value, and use the specified exact provenance map.
blockingFindings.rationale: The task explicitly fixes AggregateMetrics exact keys and provenance as a compatibility contract.

blockingFindings.title: Metric totals use sources forbidden by the aggregation contract
blockingFindings.issue: metrics() aggregates ActivityMetric.durationMs, ActivityMetric.tokens, and ActivityMetric.cost, and falls back to timing for some non-usage Activities. The contract requires measured timing/usage values and requires cost to come only from ActivityUsage.cost; the metric path also omits timing duration for some agent metrics.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Aggregate duration only from non-null ActivityTiming.durationMs, aggregate tokens and cost only from ActivityUsage fields, and keep record_metric counter handling separate without adding metric values to these totals.
blockingFindings.rationale: The current totals can report values from the wrong authority and produce incorrect nullability or sums.

blockingFindings.title: MetadataItem is an open-ended wrapper
blockingFindings.issue: MetadataItem only checks that its value is an object and applies boundedPublic(); it does not validate the required top-level or nested fields, types, or nullability.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Define MetadataItem with an explicit constructor whitelist and field-level invariants for identity, lifecycle, location, structure, relationships, timestamps, capabilities, artifacts, and metrics.
blockingFindings.rationale: T-1 requires exact metadata keys and types to be centrally managed, not merely emitted by the current projector implementation.

blockingFindings.title: ActivityItem is an open-ended wrapper
blockingFindings.issue: ActivityItem accepts any plain object and recursively bounds its values, so the Activity response contract does not centrally enforce its exact fields, nested shapes, or nullability.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Implement ActivityItem with explicit field and nested-value classes or whitelists, then serialize only the declared Activity schema.
blockingFindings.rationale: The task requires a centrally managed exact Activity item contract for consumer compatibility.

blockingFindings.title: Artifact descriptor contract is not typed
blockingFindings.issue: ArtifactDescriptorView accepts arbitrary object keys and values. The public artifact descriptor therefore has no centrally enforced exact whitelist or type/nullability invariants.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Replace the open wrapper with an explicit ArtifactDescriptor contract containing validated artifactId, metadata, activityIds, nodeIds, and taskIds fields.
blockingFindings.rationale: Artifact relationships are part of the required compatibility surface and must not depend only on the current call site's object literal.

blockingFindings.title: Resource-unknown errors omit the declared response envelope
blockingFindings.issue: When parsing fails before QueryRequest exists or resource is unknown, runFlowQueryCli emits only schemaRevision, ok, and error. It omits the resource, selectedFlowVersion, and availableFlowVersions fields needed by the defined resource-unknown error shape.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Construct a dedicated unknown-resource error response with the exact contract fields and explicit null selectedFlowVersion, using the centrally managed error schema.
blockingFindings.rationale: The acceptance criteria explicitly require a defined resource-unknown error payload and selectedFlowVersion nullability.

blockingFindings.title: Dynamic error paths are not public-safe JSON paths
blockingFindings.issue: Paths such as `/${unknown}` and `/condition/${unknownCondition}` interpolate untrusted field names without escaping `~` and `/`, so a malicious key can change the apparent path structure.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Add a central JSON Pointer token encoder and escape dynamic path segments before constructing QueryError paths.
blockingFindings.rationale: R13 requires stable public-safe error paths; unescaped user-controlled tokens make the path ambiguous and non-canonical.

blockingFindings.title: Public object collections are not bounded
blockingFindings.issue: boundedPublic() limits arrays but not the number of keys in plain objects. Large capability or nested public objects can bypass MAX_PUBLIC_COLLECTION_ITEMS and are only rejected later, if at all, by the overall response byte check.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Apply the central collection limit to Object.keys(value).length and enforce the public key constraints in boundedPublic().
blockingFindings.rationale: The task requires collection limits to be part of the shared bounded contract, including object-shaped collections.

blockingFindings.title: Metadata projection rejects its own serialized artifacts and metrics
blockingFindings.issue: metadataItem() converts ArtifactDescriptorView and AggregateMetrics instances to plain JSON before passing them to MetadataItem, whose constructor requires those exact class instances. Every metadata query therefore fails validation.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Pass the typed ArtifactDescriptorView instances and AggregateMetrics instance into MetadataItem, or have MetadataItem construct and validate those types from plain values before serialization.
blockingFindings.rationale: The required metadata success response cannot be produced by the current projector.

blockingFindings.title: NDJSON artifacts are parsed as single JSON documents
blockingFindings.issue: artifactSchemaRevision() uses mediaType.includes("json"), so application/x-ndjson activities.jsonl is sent to JSON.parse as one document. A normal multi-line Activity ledger is rejected as inconsistent during metadata projection.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Restrict schemaRevision parsing to supported single-document JSON media types, or add a separate NDJSON handling branch that does not parse the ledger as one JSON value.
blockingFindings.rationale: Valid canonical catalogs containing the required activities ledger cannot be projected into metadata.

blockingFindings.title: Unknown resources use the known-resource error payload
blockingFindings.issue: runFlowQueryCli() passes any requestedResource string to unknownResourceError(). For an unsupported resource such as "bogus", the response incorrectly includes resource, selectedFlowVersion, and availableFlowVersions instead of the generic unknown-resource shape.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Pass null to unknownResourceError() unless requestedResource is exactly metadata or activities, preserving the generic payload for unsupported resource values.
blockingFindings.rationale: The task requires a distinct payload shape for resource-unknown errors.

blockingFindings.title: AggregateMetrics accepts arbitrary provenance authorities
blockingFindings.issue: AggregateMetrics validates only that provenance has the expected keys and non-empty strings; it accepts incorrect authority values even though the contract fixes exact provenance strings for every aggregate field.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Define the required provenance map centrally and compare every supplied provenance value against its exact required string before constructing AggregateMetrics.
blockingFindings.rationale: The exported typed contract can serialize values that violate the mandatory exact provenance compatibility contract.

blockingFindings.title: Metadata derives nextAction for parked flows
blockingFindings.issue: metadataItem() calls state.nextAction() for every lifecycle except finalized, including parked flows. The canonical runtime treats nextAction as available only for active flows, so parked metadata can expose an action that is not currently runnable.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Derive next only when state.lifecycle.state === "active"; use null for parked and finalized flows.
blockingFindings.rationale: Lifecycle metadata must reflect the canonical execution boundary and must not advertise an executable route while the Flow is parked.

blockingFindings.title: Activity artifact references are silently omitted
blockingFindings.issue: QueryProjector.activityItem() resolves references only by relativePath, logicalKey, or kind:path. Canonical Activity references commonly use the artifact content digest, so artifactIds and outcome.artifactRefs are filtered out from otherwise successful responses.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Resolve references by descriptor.hash as well, map them to publicArtifactId(), and reject unresolved references as canonical inconsistency instead of silently dropping them.
blockingFindings.rationale: The ActivityItem source mapping loses durable artifact relationships and returns incomplete success data.

blockingFindings.title: Query accepts independently valid but inconsistent state and ledger
blockingFindings.issue: CanonicalFlowVersionReader validates the state structurally and parses individual ledger entries, but never applies the confirmed Activity prefix to the state or runs the journal-wide attempt/transition invariants. A state file and ledger with matching confirmation counts but different histories can therefore produce a successful response.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Route the bounded canonical inputs through the shared state/journal consistency validator or replay boundary, and reject when the replayed confirmed state does not equal the stored state.
blockingFindings.rationale: Canonical metadata and confirmed Activities must come from one consistent canonical record set; independent per-file validation is insufficient.

blockingFindings.title: Query ignores Activity ledger entries beyond the confirmed prefix
blockingFindings.issue: CanonicalFlowVersionReader.readConfirmedLedger() parses only state.confirmationOrder lines and ignores the remainder of flow.activities. A malformed, extra, or invariant-violating tail is therefore accepted, even though the canonical Flow manager rejects such a ledger.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Validate the complete bounded ledger through the shared journal parser/invariant boundary, then project only the confirmed prefix. Preserve the normal one-pending-transition rule where applicable, but reject malformed or inconsistent trailing entries.
blockingFindings.rationale: Successful query responses must be derived from a canonical state and Activity ledger that are mutually consistent; ignoring durable ledger data allows inconsistent canonical records to appear valid.

blockingFindings.title: Aggregate metrics never process Activity metric observations
blockingFindings.issue: QueryProjector.metrics() reads only ActivityUsage and ActivityTiming. It never processes ActivityMetric, so record_metric counter deltas and reset semantics are not represented and metric observations cannot be distinguished from usage for double-count prevention.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Add confirmationOrder-ordered, reset-aware processing of ActivityMetric counters at the contract’s designated projection point, while keeping ActivityUsage aggregation separate and excluding metric observations from usage totals.
blockingFindings.rationale: The task’s AggregateMetrics contract explicitly requires reset-aware record_metric accounting and forbids counting the same measurement through both metric and usage paths.

blockingFindings.title: Worktree re-execution rejects valid request-file queries
blockingFindings.issue: When a globally launched CLI re-executes in the worktree, it forwards --request-file and also pipes prepared request bytes. The child sees both stdin and --request-file and returns INVALID_REQUEST for an otherwise valid request-file invocation.
blockingFindings.suggestion: When queryInput is handed to executeWorktreeLocalCli(), remove the --request-file option/value from the child argv, or preserve the original input mode instead of supplying both sources.
blockingFindings.rationale: The query contract accepts either stdin or --request-file; valid request-file queries must remain valid across the mandated worktree-local CLI boundary.

blockingFindings.title: Query uses the invocation directory instead of the shared repository-root resolver
blockingFindings.issue: repositoryRoot() falls back directly to process.cwd(), unlike the shared repoRoot() resolver that discovers the Git repository root. Invoking the local CLI from a nested project directory therefore searches for specs below that directory and can report SPEC_NOT_FOUND.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Use the shared repoRoot() or equivalent project-context resolver in repositoryRoot(), while retaining SENNEL_WORK_ROOT as the explicit override.
blockingFindings.rationale: The query command must locate canonical Flow Versions using the project root established by the CLI’s normal command architecture.

blockingFindings.title: Query limits and error codes are not shared with fixture and consumer compatibility surfaces
blockingFindings.issue: FLOW_QUERY_LIMITS and FLOW_QUERY_ERROR_CODES are defined in src/flow/query.js and used by the CLI, but the added integration test hardcodes INVALID_REQUEST and does not consume the limits; no shared fixture or consumer compatibility test is added.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Expose the contract from a central query-contract module and import its error codes and limits from the CLI, canonical fixture, and consumer compatibility test.
blockingFindings.rationale: Acceptance requires the error-code set and collection/byte limits to be shared across CLI, fixture, and consumer compatibility validation.

blockingFindings.title: Worktree re-execution rejects valid request-file queries
blockingFindings.issue: The parent prepares --request-file content, then re-executes with the original --request-file arguments while also piping the same bytes as stdin. The child therefore detects both input sources and returns INVALID_REQUEST.
blockingFindings.suggestion: When passing queryInput to the local CLI, remove --request-file and its value from argv, or preserve request-file mode and omit queryInput.

blockingFindings.title: Metadata nextAction uses the current cursor instead of the selected action path
blockingFindings.issue: metadataItem() populates nextAction.stepId and taskId from currentPath. For a fresh flow currentPath is empty, and for recovery actions next.path may differ from currentPath, so the reported next action has incorrect or null target identifiers.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Derive nextAction.stepId and taskId from next.path/next.node, independently of the current location projection.
blockingFindings.rationale: Metadata source mapping must identify the canonical action selected by CurrentFlowState.nextAction(), including fresh and recovery routes.

blockingFindings.title: Artifact metadata assigns static flow nodes to nonexistent tasks
blockingFindings.issue: artifactDescriptor() infers taskId with a suffix regex. Static nodes such as spec-review or impl-gate are therefore reported as tasks named spec or impl even though they are flow-level nodes.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Derive taskIds from canonical state ancestry and emit them only when the associated Activity node is inside a materialized TaskNode; otherwise return an empty taskIds list.
blockingFindings.rationale: ArtifactDescriptor relationships must reflect canonical task ownership rather than treating arbitrary node-name suffixes as task identities.

blockingFindings.title: Available-version discovery only recognizes three-digit directories
blockingFindings.issue: listAvailableVersions() filters directory names with /^\d{3}$/, while FlowVersion accepts any positive safe integer and pathSegment emits four or more digits for versions above 999.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Parse all decimal version directory names accepted by FlowVersion and retain the bounded count check.
blockingFindings.rationale: The request contract accepts positive Flow Version integers, so discovery must not make valid canonical versions unreachable.

blockingFindings.rationale: Successful responses must derive from mutually consistent canonical state and Activity authorities; unchecked ledger content can expose inconsistent canonical records.

blockingFindings.title: Aggregate metrics never process Activity metric observations
blockingFindings.issue: CurrentFlowActivitySummary.metrics() reads timing and ActivityUsage only. It never processes confirmed record_metric observations or reset-aware counter deltas.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Process confirmed record_metric Activities in confirmationOrder order with reset-aware delta handling, while keeping metric and usage measurements separate to prevent double counting.
blockingFindings.rationale: The contract explicitly requires reset-aware record_metric accounting and non-overlapping usage and metric measurements.

blockingFindings.title: Query error codes and limits are not consumed by fixtures or compatibility tests
blockingFindings.issue: The test hard-codes INVALID_REQUEST and page size values and no touched fixture or consumer compatibility test imports FLOW_QUERY_ERROR_CODES or FLOW_QUERY_LIMITS.
blockingFindings.suggestion: Import the centralized query contract constants in the fixture and compatibility tests, and assert error codes and boundary values through those shared fields.
blockingFindings.rationale: T-1 requires the error-code set and collection/byte limits to be shared across the CLI, fixtures, and consumer compatibility tests so contract changes cannot silently drift.
